A newborn is evaluated in the hospital nursery one hour after birth. The infant was delivered at term by
a 27-year-old G2P2 mother following an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, with Apgar scores of 9
at both 1 and 5 minutes. There is no significant family medical history. The newborn's weight and
length are at the 50th percentile, with normal vital signs. Physical examination reveals
female-appearing external genitalia with an enlarged clitoris, and bilateral firm masses are detected on
inguinal palpation. Pelvic ultrasound shows absence of uterus and ovaries. Laboratory studies indicate
normal serum levels of luteinizing hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, estradiol, and testosterone.
Genetic testing reveals a 46,XY karyotype. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome (B) Mixed gonadal dysgenesis (C) Aromatase deficiency (D)
Complete gonadal dysgenesis (E) Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (F) Androgen insensitivity syndrome
(G) True hermaphroditism (H) Leydig cell hypoplasia (I) 5α-reductase deficiency (J) Ovotesticular
disorder of sex development
 A. Complete gonadal dysgenesis
B. Ovotesticular disorder of sex development
C. 5α-reductase deficiency
D. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
E. Androgen insensitivity syndrome
F. True hermaphroditism
G. Persistent Müllerian duct syndrome
H. Mixed gonadal dysgenesis
I. Leydig cell hypoplasia
J. Aromatase deficiency
